decision.summary: The tenant called a rotten-egg boiler smell "not urgent", but it is a suspected gas leak with an 82-year-old in the flat, so it is an emergency. I sent safety instructions, opened emergency job JOB-102, assigned HeatRight (Gas Safe, out of hours), escalated P1 and told the landlord.

answers.question: What severity is this and why?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is a suspected gas leak whatever the tenant says, and an 82-year-old is staying there.

answers.question: What exactly do you tell the tenant right now?
answers.answer: In order: get everyone out, with the 82-year-old out first; no switches, flames or boiler, and open doors and windows if safe; call 0800 111 999 (999 if anyone is unwell); are the CO alarm or any symptoms present; reply to confirm everyone is out; an engineer is being sent tonight; don't go back in until told it is safe.

answers.question: Which actions do you take tonight?
answers.answer: Created emergency job JOB-102 linked to R-4801. Assigned HeatRight Ltd for a same-night make-safe without waiting for landlord approval. Escalated P1 (ESC-103). Emailed landlord Ben afterwards.

args.body: Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler can be a gas leak, so please treat it as urgent tonight. Please: 1) Get everyone out of the flat now, including your flatmate's mum (82), who should go out first with help. 2) Don't use light switches, flames, or the boiler. If it's safe, open doors and windows on your way out. 3) Once outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24h). Call 999 if anyone feels unwell. 4) Is your kitchen CO alarm sounding? Does anyone have a headache, dizziness, nausea or drowsiness? 5) Please reply to confirm everyone is out. We're sending a Gas Safe engineer out tonight to make it safe. Please don't go back in until they or the gas emergency service say it's safe.
